To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the caged analogues of cADPR, NAADP, and IP3 are useful tools for the study of the photogeneration of these intracellular calcium mobilizing molecules.
cADPR and cADP-riboside are synthesized by ADP-ribo- cyclase, and NAADP is generated by ADP- ribosyl cyclase-catalyzed exchange between NAD+ and nicotinic acids.
we have developed caged cADPR and caged NAADP, and characterized their photolysis, and demonstrated their use in generating intracellular Ca2+ signals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the photogeneration of two novel intracellular Ca2+-mobilizing agents, cyclic ADP-riboses (cADP-ribo) and nicotinate-adenine dinucleotide-phosphate (NAADP), from photolabile precursors.

the development of caged analogs of the Ca2+-releasing second messengers cyclic ADP-ribose and nicotinic adenine dinucleotides, which are used in studies of Ca2+ mobilization and Ca2+-dependent processes.
developing new methods for the synthesis and characterization of the caged precursors of caged cADPR and caged NAADP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
photolysis of the caged analogs is an excellent tool for studying the role of calcium mobilization in cellular processes.
the cADPR and NADP caged derivatives are useful tools for the characterization of the role of cADPR in intracellular Ca2+ mobilization.
the photolysis of caged cADPR and caged NAADP is an effective and versatile means of generating these calcium mobilizing agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a general strategy for the photolysis of NPE phosphates and demonstrated that the photolysis can be used to generate caged analogs of cADPR or NAADP.
caged cADPR and caged NAADP are useful tools to study the role of these signaling molecules in the regulation of calcium signaling in cells.
the photogeneration of caged cADPR and caged NAADP is an efficient, rapid, and reliable method to generate cADPR and/or NAADP in a controlled fashion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
photogeneration of cADPR from its caged analog can be used to induce a transient elevation of intracellular calcium concentration in a variety of cell types.
the photolysis of cADPR- and NAADP-NPE is fast and efficient, and the products are stable under conditions where they can be assayed.
the photogeneration of cADPR or NAADP can be achieved with high efficiency, high specificity, and low phototoxicity.
